title: Cost-synthesis workload prober and safe optimizer
creator: Priya Nair
description: Goal: Build a lightweight workload prober and continuous optimizer that synthesizes batching and prefix/KV cache recommendations per-customer and per-route, and applies changes using a staged canary/rollback flow.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Profiler collects 7-day signature histograms and per-route prefix-hit rates with <5% overhead. 2) Heuristic composer proposes batch_size, max_wait_ms, and kv_cache_window per route; simulated cost delta vs baseline computed. 3) Safe-apply pipeline supports shadow rollouts, micro-canary (0.1% traffic), gradual ramp to 10%, auto-rollback on SLO regressions or cost regressions beyond thresholds. 4) Console shows recommendation rationale and per-customer preview prior to apply.
implementation_notes: Architecture: (a) lightweight probe runs as cron in infra that samples live traffic traces into anonymized signatures; (b) offline synthesizer runs heuristics + simulated coalescing model to estimate latency and cost deltas; (c) continuous annealer tunes parameters during low-traffic windows and records telemetry. Key heuristics: prefix-length aware batching, kv-window sensitivity (shorter windows for high-entropy workloads), sequence-length bucketing, and conservative TTL for initial apply. Safety: use golden prompt-set on canary traffic for quality regression checks, and enforce SLO guardrails via tracing-based latency percentiles and error-rate thresholds.
tradeoffs_and_decisions: - We prioritize conservative recommendations: initial applies bias towards smaller batch increases to avoid tail-latency regressions. - Use simulated coalescing model rather than fully online experiments for the majority of suggestions to reduce blast radius. - Decided to keep per-customer profiles for high-volume tenants and use aggregated profiles for small tenants to limit storage/compute cost. - KV-caching recommendations are gated behind an opt-in flag because of potential semantic effects with stateful tool-calling workflows.
comments: 2026-02-20: Ticket created by Priya Nair. Proposal pitched in engineering sync; documented initial scope in Confluence (link below).

2026-02-25: Spike complete: sampling agent prototype can collect signature+prefix stats at ~2% CPU on serving nodes. Profiling microbenchmark in /confluence/CostOps/WorkloadProberSpike shows data shapes.

2026-03-01: Design review with PM + Design (Marco Velez, Asha Raman). Feedback: expose human-readable rationale strings for console (e.g., 'expected 14% token cost reduction for route X; 95th latency increase risk 0.3%'). Need opt-out flag for tenant-level experimentation.

2026-03-04: Implementation started. Created proto synthesizer service: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pulls/4582. Initial heuristics include: min_batch=1, max_batch=128, wait_ms defaults derived from p95 inter-arrival time.
2026-03-07: QA note from Maya O'Connor: golden-set comparisons must include stochastic seed controls for model variance. Added deterministic sampling for eval harness.

2026-03-10: Canary plan drafted: 0.1% shadow -> 0.1% live -> 1% live -> 10% live, with auto-rollback triggers: p95 latency > baseline + 10ms OR error-rate > baseline * 1.5 OR cost delta positive beyond 5% for sustained 10 minutes. Shared to #infra-cost-ops for feedback.

2026-03-12: Interim telemetry: simulated runs on last-week profile show median token-cost reduction 9.8% for top 10 routes, estimated 1.5% overall platform cost improvement if applied selectively. Leaving note to instrument per-tenant net-cost dashboard widget before any wide apply.
Next steps: finish console UI PR, add tenant opt-in toggle, implement auto-rollback monitor, schedule canary on staging cluster.
qa_and_risks: QA: run shadow canary on staging 48h, compare golden-set outputs and latency percentiles. Risks: model output variance causing false positives in quality checks; KV-cache config changes may change semantics for some tool-calling prompts. Mitigations: seed control for golden set, tenant opt-out, rollback thresholds conservative.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: shadow apply for 48h (all routes). Phase 1: micro-canary (0.1% traffic) on 10 low-risk routes. Phase 2: ramp to 10% for selected high-win routes. Phase 3: broader apply with tenant preview and admin approval. Auto-rollback on SLO or cost anomalies. Manual override in Console for urgent rollback.
notes_for_reviewers: Please check safety thresholds (latency + error + cost) and suggest alternate default values if your team owns high-sensitivity routes. Review PR #4582 for synthesizer code and PR #2125 for Console changes. Special attention: privacy of sampled signatures — data is anonymized and hashed, but security review can be enabled if needed.
